spec.verdict:
PROCEED. Merged design = Design 3's diagnosis + Design 1's state machine + Design 2's role contracts, corrected on the one decision all three got partly wrong.

VERIFIED AGAINST REAL CODE (/Users/roy/Documents/mc-wizard @ 7ebbbe8, src/wizard.mjs = 5319 lines, npm test = 572/572 green in 9.3s):

V1. THE #44 FIX IS INERT ON THE EXACT LIVE STRING, AND ITS TEST IS SELF-BLINDING. src/wizard.mjs:104-107 uses (?:can|could)(?:n['’]t| not); after "can" is consumed the group demands a leading n, so it only matches the nonexistent "cann't". Measured: "I can't safely clear a 50x50 area..." -> false; "I cannot do that." -> false; "I can not do that." -> true; "I couldn't" -> true. The regression test at test/wizard.test.mjs:3694-3718 asserts with the SAME defective regex, so it is green while the bug ships. Only Design 3 found this. It is the highest-value single line in the brief.

V2. BOTH LIVE TURNS STILL REPRODUCE TODAY (ran end-to-end, corpus stubbed empty):
 Turn 1 (provider refuses) -> action null, mode "chat:model", answer = the bare refusal VERBATIM.
 Turn 2 (provider promises) -> throws at 5079, lands in the offline catch 5156-5166, ships action null, mode "offline-fallback".
 classifyAction returns null for both questions.

V3. GATING DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED. Every contract/repair/floor site (5097, 5136, 5174, 5179, 5181) is lexically inside buildRequest. isBuildRequest (1980-1994) is false for terrain. The floor is structurally unreachable.

V4. DESIGN 3'S "FACT 3" IS RIGHT AND SPLITS ACROSS TWO TIERS. One identical valid run_commands fill-with-air, eight phrasings:
 ACCEPT "clear a 50x50 area around me, starting at the ground beneath this tree"
 ACCEPT "wiz can you clear the trees around here" / "remove all blocks in a 50x50 area"
 REJECT gate=intent-match: "just level the ground, remove all blocks in a 50x50 area" (the real turn 2), "flatten this hill please", "dig out a big hole here", "level the ground here", "make this flat"
Isolating sub-gates: "flatten this hill"/"level the ground here" fail the SAFETY tier (providerPowerMatchesRequest fill-with-air intent at 3338-3341 lacks level|flatten|smooth). "just level the ground, remove all blocks..." and "dig out a big hole here" fail the PHRASING tier (the clause-verb whitelist at 3437, plus requestClauses at 70-73 not splitting on commas).

V5. THE DECISION ALL THREE GOT PARTLY WRONG. Design 3 argued a deterministic terrain rung must NOT go in classifyAction because providerActionMatchesRequest:3431 would force byte-equality. Design 1 called that a bonus. Both missed the ordering that settles it. The run_commands branch is: providerPowerMatchesRequest FIRST (3430), then the classified byte-equality return (3431), then the phrasing whitelist (3433-3441). Therefore a deterministic terrain rung SKIPS the phrasing tier entirely, and the deterministic action itself never passes through either gate. I verified that deterministic rungs already do exactly this: commandAction (1605-1633) emits allowedWizardAction({type:"run_commands",...,commands:["effect @s ... "]}) which reaches selectedAction at 4915 with NO providerActionMatchesRequest and NO providerPowerMatchesRequest call. Those gates exist to police MODEL-authored power, not code-authored rungs.
CONSEQUENCE: Design 3's M6 is UNNECESSARY AND MUST BE DROPPED. We do NOT widen the safety gate at 3338-3341 and we do NOT widen the phrasing whitelist at 3437. The terrain fix requires ZERO edits to any safety regex. This is strictly the safest of the three proposals and I am adopting it.

V6. A GAP ALL THREE DESIGNS MISSED. The offer floor cannot bind for terrain. answerOffersAction (109-111) and offeredActionQuestion (113-116) carry the pre-#42 constructive-only verb list. Measured: "I can level the ground around you." -> false; "I can dig out a 20x20 pit here." -> false. So pendingActionTurn never matches and a bare "yes" never binds. #42 widened answerPromisesAction with terrain verbs but left these two behind. Symmetry repair is mandatory or the terminal rung ping-pongs.

V7. COST GATE INTACT AND MEASURABLE. fetchImpl call counter, 7 canned turns, all 0 provider calls: "hello wizard"/"thanks!"/"tell me a joke" -> local-instant; "build a t flip flop"/"build an automatic chicken farm" -> local-skill place_blueprint; "teleport me to the nether" -> local-skill dimension_travel; "give me 64 torches" -> local-skill give_items.

V8. FILL ARITHMETIC. Bedrock per-fill cap 32768. A 50x50 footprint is 51x51 = 2601 blocks/layer, so max 12 y-layers per command (31212 blocks); 13 layers = 33813 and would fail. Design 1's "13 layers" is wrong by one. skills.mjs:257-262 caps run_commands at 8 commands, each single-line and <=500 chars via normalizeRequesterCommand (capability-runtime.js:65-69). The pack executes via execute as @a[tag=...] at @s run <cmd> (main.js:5641) so ~ is requester-relative, and runCommandsForPlayer (main.js:5650-5670) already degrades gracefully to "partial" rather than nothing. run_commands is in EXECUTOR_VERIFIED_ACTION_TYPES (3465), so terrain work costs ZERO post-execution provider review.

V9. parseRequestedDimensions IS exported (wizard.mjs:222) and returns {width:50,depth:50} for both live questions, {width:20,depth:20} for "clear a 20 by 20 space", undefined for "flatten this hill".

V10. NO EXISTING TEST PINS THE MODEL-AUTHORED TERRAIN FILL. Grep of all four test files referencing run_commands shows no assertion on terrain acceptance. Exactly one existing test must change: the self-blinding #44 test. No safety test changes.

WHAT I REJECT FROM THE INPUTS: Design 3's C4 model critic (new per-turn provider cost, unprovable offline) is cut entirely. Design 3's M6 vocabulary widenings are cut (V5). Design 1's isBuildRequest suppression-list edit is cut in favour of terrainAction self-bailing on explicitlyRequestsBuild, which closes the "clear the ground and build a castle" two-way door without touching isBuildRequest. All three designs' proposal to collapse the six recursive api.ask calls is deferred: it changes sessions.reserve counts and therefore supersede semantics, and the owner cannot live-test this week.
spec.architecture:
ROLE MODULES (all new files under src/roles/, dependency-free ESM, Node >=22.9, no new npm package). Every role is a FACTORY taking its validated dependencies by injection, so no role imports src/wizard.mjs and no import cycle exists. src/wizard.mjs keeps every validated predicate exactly where it is today and hands them to the roles.

1. TurnState - src/roles/turn-state.mjs
createTurnState({answer, action, responseMode, title}). Owns the seven closure mutables ask() rewrites out of order (answer 4908, selectedAction 4915, providerGoal, providerActionAccepted 4919, contractCaveat 4936, title 4920, responseMode 4921) plus gateTrace/recordRejection/gateError (4939-4949). ONE invariant: responseMode and action are written through a single adopt() pair so they cannot drift - that drift is what main.js:6391 (planning-deferred retry) keys on and no Node test would catch it. Pure data, no Minecraft knowledge.

2. TurnIntent - src/roles/intent.mjs
createIntent(deps).describe({question, history, actionHistory, context, general, flags}) -> a FROZEN record. Verbatim relocation of wizard.mjs:4849-4935. Adds exactly two fields:
 - actionableIntent = buildRequest || projectFeedback || terrainIntent || adminIntent || travelIntent || giftIntent || effectIntent. This is the generalization of buildRequest that unlocks the floor.
 - consultModel = the askModel expression from 4931-4935 copied CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER. It is the sole cost gate and is computed in exactly one place.
Delegates to isBuildRequest, isProjectFeedback, isRecipeRequest, isGoalSatisfaction, isOrdinaryConversation, instantConversationAnswer, groundedQuickAnswer, retrievalQuestion, wantsModelAuthoredStructure, hasUnmatchedDescriptors, boundPendingOffer, historyWithObservedStructure. No predicate is altered; buildRequest keeps its exact current definition so every existing build test is untouched.

3. TerrainPlanner - src/roles/terrain.mjs
createTerrainPlanner({parseRequestedDimensions, allowedWizardAction, explicitlyRequestsBuild, explicitlyRequestsCommand, isRecipeRequest, isOrdinaryConversation}) -> {terrainIntent, terrainAction}.
terrainIntent(question) -> {width, depth, mode:'clear'|'level'} | null. Requires a terrain VERB (clear|level|flatten|remove|dig|excavate|smooth|demolish|erase|wipe) AND a terrain/area NOUN (area|ground|space|patch|land|hill|terrain|dirt|blocks|trees|region|plot) in the SAME clause, AND an imperative/request framing. Returns null on explicitlyRequestsBuild, explicitlyRequestsCommand, isRecipeRequest, isOrdinaryConversation, or an interrogative framing ("what happens if I dig straight down").
terrainAction(question) -> action | null. Emits {type:"run_commands", version:1, commands:[...]} of y-sliced `fill ~-H ~L ~-H ~H ~U ~H air`, then RE-VALIDATES through allowedWizardAction and returns its output, never the raw object.
Geometry: footprint clamped to 64x64 (half-extent 32); default vertical window feet(~0) to ~+11 = 12 layers, which for a 51x51 footprint is 31212 blocks, under the 32768 per-fill cap (V8) and one single command. Larger windows chunk into at most 8 commands. Any clamp emits a contract caveat; it never silently shrinks.
Wired as a classifyAction rung placed AFTER the `if (refusesBuild) return null` bail and after the pending-offer resume, immediately before worldControlAction. Placement after refusesBuild is load-bearing: it keeps "just explain how to clear a 50x50 area" from producing a fill.

4. Critic - src/roles/critic.mjs
createCritic({allowedWizardAction, safeNovelAction, providerActionMatchesRequest, actionCompletesBuildRequest, actionAdvancesBuildRequest, correctiveActionContinuesGoal, unusableWizardAnswer, answerPromisesAction, answerRefusesAction, plannerRepairDetail}).critique(candidate, intent) -> Verdict {ok, severity:'fatal'|'contract'|'warning'|'none', tier, gate, reason, warning?, repairDetail?}.
FOUR TIERS, fixed order, short-circuit on first non-'none':
 C0 SAFETY (severity 'fatal', never repaired toward, never hinted, never overridable): allowedWizardAction non-null; safeNovelAction when researchRequired (verbatim rejection text "web-researched build plans cannot contain server administration or arbitrary commands"); unusableWizardAnswer on prose.
 C1 EXISTENCE (severity 'contract') - THE GATE THAT DOES NOT EXIST TODAY: !action && (intent.actionableIntent || answerPromisesAction(answer) || answerRefusesAction(answer)). The FIRST disjunct is the structural fix: it fires on the live session regardless of what prose the model produced, so the never-empty property does NOT depend on getting a refusal regex right. The other two disjuncts are defense in depth.
 C2 FIDELITY (severity 'contract'): providerActionMatchesRequest called WHOLE and unchanged (see Risks - it is NOT physically split; the Critic records which sub-gate fired for telemetry only).
 C3 COMPLETENESS: actionCompletesBuildRequest for intentClass build/project-feedback. TRI-STATE IS LOAD-BEARING: true -> 'none'; {complete:false, warning} -> severity 'warning' with warning carried on the Verdict; false -> 'contract'. Plus actionAdvancesBuildRequest. Verdict.severity is a four-value enum from day one so no boundary can coerce it to boolean.
NO C4 MODEL CRITIC. Cut for cost discipline and offline provability.

5. Escalator - src/roles/escalation.mjs
createEscalator(rungs).next(escalationIndex, intent, ctx, rejectedRungs) -> {rung, candidate} | null. Unifies today's two divergent floor sites (5136, 5181) into one ordered ladder, preserving both existing orderings exactly.

6. Orchestrator - src/roles/orchestrator.mjs
createOrchestrator({planners, critic, escalator, budget, recordRejection}).runTurn(intent, state) -> the terminal TurnState. Owns transitions, budgets, and the terminal assertUsefulOutcome. Contains no regex, no Minecraft vocabulary, no allowlist - so it is unit-testable with fake roles and can never widen a safety boundary.
ADJUDICATION RULE for planner-vs-critic disagreement: C0 -> critic wins unconditionally, action dropped, escalate. C1/C2 -> one repair round if budget remains, else escalate. C3 severity 'warning' -> ORCHESTRATOR OVERRULES THE CRITIC and ships with contractCaveat set and a 'complete' providerGoal downgraded to 'active' (today's 5149-5154, unchanged). That last rule is the cost story: partial credit goes to the world, where the existing post-execution evaluator finishes the argument, not to another provider round.

WHAT STAYS IN src/wizard.mjs, UNMOVED: every validated predicate (allowedWizardAction is in skills.mjs and is UNTOUCHED), intake, the player-preference short-circuit (4816-4835), sessions.reserve (4847), corpus retrieval, preference application (5204-5215), the memory notice, goalForTurn (484-508) and the goalId resolution ladder (5254-5257), the supersede check and persistence (5272-5298), the final unsafeCommandAnswer scrub (5224-5226) which MUST stay the last transform on answer, recordActionResult, recordFeedback. Leave a comment at the extraction boundary stating that moving persistence or goalId into the orchestrator would silently break recordActionResult's supersede logic (4712-4718), the 6-action cap (4728) and the 3-failure cap (4786).

UNTOUCHED BY DESIGN: src/skills.mjs (already the pure gatekeeper), src/server.mjs (response contract unchanged), src/sessions.mjs, src/command-safety.mjs, src/learned-recipes.mjs, and EVERY file under bedrock/behavior_packs/**. No new action type, no new response mode, no change to the {review, replan, retry, reviewDeferred, reviewLimitReached, retryLimitReached, superseded, updated, replayed} vocabulary main.js:335-403 dispatches on. run_commands already has an executor arm (main.js:6301).

TURN STATE MACHINE (src/roles/orchestrator.mjs):
 START -> SHORTCUT when !intent.consultModel ; -> CONSULT when intent.consultModel
 SHORTCUT: state already carries the deterministic/learned action. -> CRITIQUE if action ; -> CRITIQUE with a null candidate if !action && intent.actionableIntent (C1 fires) ; -> FINALIZE otherwise
 CONSULT: run the provider planner. ANY throw (envelope parse, unusable answer, transport, timeout) is caught HERE, recorded via gateError, and transitions to ESCALATE - NOT to the current blanket reset at 5156-5166 whose `selectedAction = safeFallback.action` is literally what erased the live terrain turn. -> ANSWER_ONLY when answerOnlyRequest (gate 4971-4978, then FINALIZE) ; -> REVIEW when reviewRequest ; -> CRITIQUE otherwise
 REVIEW: the verdict gate 5086-5096 unchanged. complete-with-no-action -> FINALIZE. corrective-continuing -> CRITIQUE. neither -> ESCALATE (today this throws).
 CRITIQUE: severity 'none' -> FINALIZE. 'warning' -> set contractCaveat, downgrade goal, FINALIZE. 'contract' + budget -> REPAIR. 'contract' no budget, or 'fatal' -> ESCALATE. The recipe-request override (5061-5070) and the informational-repair branch (5008-5059) are two named early edges, not new logic.
 REPAIR: repairPlannerAction with the SHARED budget object. accepted -> CRITIQUE (re-critiqued, never trusted). exhausted -> ESCALATE.
 ESCALATE: escalationIndex += 1, rejected rung appended to rejectedRungs and never re-produced. -> CRITIQUE for rungs that yield an action ; R6 is the sole rung that bypasses CRITIQUE because it ships no action. -> FINALIZE.
 FINALIZE: canonicalizeGeneratedPlanKind (5171-5173), actionAdvancesBuildRequest final null-out (5174-5178) which may re-enter ESCALATE AT MOST ONCE (tracked by a boolean), then assertUsefulOutcome unconditionally, then return.

BUDGETS - folded into the existing caps, never stacked. Provider consults per turn stay at today's ceiling: 1 planning consult (2 transport attempts, 4207) + at most 1 informational repair (5030) + repairRounds <= MC_WIZARD_REPAIR_ROUNDS (default 2, clamp 1-4, 3671) under ONE cumulative MC_WIZARD_REPAIR_BUDGET_MS wall clock (default 90s, 3676). The budget is a single object constructed by the Orchestrator and passed BY REFERENCE into repairPlannerAction so its existing Date.now()-startedAt check at 3684-3688 is the only clock. escalationIndex <= 6, strictly increasing. Cross-turn budgets (MAX_AUTOMATIC_GOAL_ACTIONS=6 at 3464, failures>=3 at 4786, main.js planningAttempt<2 at 6394, 4x429 retries at 6372, 3 action-result attempts at main.js:313) are OUTSIDE this loop and untouched. sessions.reserve still fires EXACTLY ONCE per ask(); the whole loop is inside one reservation, so a longer ladder cannot mint extra sequences and supersede semantics are provably unchanged.

ESCALATION LADDER (one ordered list, selected by intent; every rung is re-critiqued, a rung never self-accepts):
 R0 accepted planner action (provider or verified learned recipe).
 R1 classifyAction(question, actionHistory) - today's #44 ladder at 5074-5085, now reached on ANY C1 verdict rather than only when prose trips a regex, and TRANSITIONING instead of throwing.
 R2 provisionalRecipeAction - build turns only. Must keep outranking R3 exactly as it does at both current sites (5136, 5181).
 R3 localStructureFallback (3786-3803) - build turns only, internals UNTOUCHED: commonFarmAction -> projectFeedbackFallback -> stagedMachineProgressAction -> structureAction -> stagedBuildProgressAction ONLY as a continuation (priorStagedStructureProgress guard at 3771) -> proceduralStructureAction as the terminal. Because proceduralStructureAction is total for build turns, BUILD TURN BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED by this work.
 R4 terrainAction - fires when intent.terrainIntent is set. This is the rung the live session needed and that does not exist today.
 R5 BOUND CLARIFICATION - one in-character sentence naming ONE concrete executable next step derived from the question, recorded as a pending offer. Three contract properties, each separately tested: (a) satisfies answerOffersAction but NOT answerPromisesAction and NOT answerRefusesAction; (b) is NOT a capability menu, so it dodges the deliberate non-binding shapes at 141-142 and pendingActionTurn/boundPendingOffer (124, 136-149) resolve it, making the next bare "yes" EXECUTE; (c) is built FROM the ladder's own capability, never from free prose, so it can only ever offer something a rung can actually produce.
 R6 PLANNING_DEFERRED_ANSWER with mode 'planning-deferred' - byte-identical to today, already retried once by main.js:6390-6394. Terminal, pure, no provider, no failure mode.
NON-ACTIONABLE TURNS (conversation, answer-only, recipe, review) have an EMPTY ladder and finalize with prose exactly as today. An honest "I don't know" on a knowledge question is the CORRECT outcome and must not become a build. This is why the widening is actionableIntent and not "every turn".

workPackages.title: Tiered Critic (pure, parallel-safe)
workPackages.spec:
createCritic(deps).critique(candidate, intent) -> Verdict. Zero I/O, zero closure over ask() state, all validators injected. Four tiers C0 SAFETY / C1 EXISTENCE / C2 FIDELITY / C3 COMPLETENESS in fixed order, short-circuiting on the first non-'none'. Verdict.severity is a four-value enum ('fatal'|'contract'|'warning'|'none') from the first commit so no boundary can flatten the tri-state.
C1 is keyed on intent.actionableIntent FIRST and on the promise/refusal regexes only as defense in depth - this is what makes the never-empty property independent of getting a refusal regex right.
C2 calls providerActionMatchesRequest WHOLE and UNCHANGED. It is NOT physically split into a safety half and a phrasing half; the Critic merely records which sub-gate fired, for telemetry. Splitting it across six call sites (4990, 3711, 4896 and the classifyAction-adjacent paths) risks a candidate being safety-checked twice and fidelity-checked zero times.
repairDetail is produced by the existing plannerRepairDetail (3604) and never re-derived, preserving the coupled truncation budget chain plannerRepairDetail(2000) / wizardActionRejection (skills.mjs:310) / turnDetailLimit 2048 (4072).
NO model critic tier. Explicitly out of scope for cost discipline and offline provability.

spec.invariantProof:
THE INVARIANT. For any turn where intent.actionableIntent is true, ask() returns either (a) a non-null action, or (b) an answer that is a bound offer - satisfying answerOffersAction, failing answerPromisesAction and answerRefusesAction, and not matching the deliberately-non-binding menu shapes at wizard.mjs:141-142 - or (c) mode 'planning-deferred', which main.js:6390-6394 already retries. It NEVER returns a bare refusal, an empty promise, or a corpus excerpt.

WHY THE CURRENT CODE VIOLATES IT (measured, not inferred). Three independent holes, all confirmed by running the real turns:
 H1. The refusal detector at 104-107 does not fire on "can't" or "cannot", so the #44 ladder at 5074-5085 is never entered for the live sentence and the refusal ships verbatim (observed: action null, mode "chat:model").
 H2. When the ladder IS entered and classifyAction returns null - which it does for both live questions - line 5079 THROWS. The universal catch at 5156-5166 then executes `selectedAction = safeFallback.action`, and safeFallback.action is the same null classifyAction already produced. The catch does not recover; it launders the failure into a shipped empty turn (observed: action null, mode "offline-fallback").
 H3. Every floor is lexically inside `if (buildRequest ...)` (5136, 5179, 5181) and isBuildRequest is false for terrain, so no floor is reachable at all.

WHERE THE NEW DESIGN ENFORCES IT - three layers, the first of which is the structural one:

LAYER 1 - DETECTION IS NOT REGEX-DEPENDENT. Critic tier C1 EXISTENCE fires on `!action && intent.actionableIntent` as its FIRST disjunct. The promise and refusal regexes are only the second and third disjuncts. Therefore H1 cannot recur even if a future refusal phrasing escapes every regex: the trigger is the CLASSIFICATION of the request, which is computed from the child's question, not from the model's prose. This is the single most important structural property in the spec and it is why I adopted Design 3's C1 over Design 1's regex-driven assertion. (The regexes are still repaired in A1 as defense in depth and because the live bug is real.)

LAYER 2 - THE LADDER IS TOTAL AND TERMINATING. ESCALATE walks R0..R6 with a monotonically increasing escalationIndex and an append-only rejectedRungs set, so no rung is re-litigated and the walk is bounded by 7. R6 (PLANNING_DEFERRED_ANSWER) is a pure local constant requiring no provider, no parser, and no world state - it has no failure mode and therefore always yields a value. R5 immediately precedes it and is a pure string constructor built FROM the ladder's own capability. Therefore ESCALATE is a TOTAL function: for every input it returns a non-empty outcome. H2 is closed by construction because the throw at 5079 and the throw at 5145 are deleted and replaced by transitions into this total function, and because the outer try/catch body is changed from `selectedAction = safeFallback.action` (which launders failure into emptiness) to a transition into ESCALATE.

LAYER 3 - THE TERMINAL ASSERTION. The state machine has EXACTLY ONE terminal state, FINALIZE. Every outgoing edge of every state - SHORTCUT, CONSULT, ANSWER_ONLY, REVIEW, CRITIQUE, REPAIR, ESCALATE - leads either to FINALIZE or to a state strictly closer to it, and the sole back-edge (FINALIZE -> ESCALATE, taken when actionAdvancesBuildRequest nulls a late action) is guarded by a boolean and fires at most once. The caught-exception path also lands in FINALIZE. FINALIZE runs assertUsefulOutcome UNCONDITIONALLY as its last step:
  if (intent.actionableIntent && !state.action
      && !(answerOffersAction(state.answer) && !isMenuShape(state.answer))
      && state.responseMode !== 'planning-deferred')
    -> replace state.answer with the R5 bound-offer text, set responseMode 'local-offer-floor', recordRejection('offer-floor', ...)
Because FINALIZE is the unique terminal state and assertUsefulOutcome is unconditional within it, there is NO path out of runTurn that skips the assertion. H3 is closed because the gate on the whole ladder and on the assertion is actionableIntent, not buildRequest.

TERMINATION. Both loop counters (escalationIndex, repairRoundsUsed) are monotonically increasing integers with hard ceilings (7 and MC_WIZARD_REPAIR_ROUNDS <= 4). Every transition either increments one of them or moves to FINALIZE. The single back-edge fires at most once. Provider rungs additionally cannot run once the shared MC_WIZARD_REPAIR_BUDGET_MS wall clock is spent. Therefore runTurn terminates in at most 7 transitions even with a provider that is down, hung, or adversarial - and it terminates in FINALIZE, where the assertion runs.

SCOPE - WHY THIS IS NOT "ALWAYS SAY SOMETHING UPBEAT". The invariant is gated on actionableIntent. For conversation, answer-only, recipe and review turns the ladder is EMPTY and the assertion does not fire, so an honest "I don't know that yet" still ships with action null. test/wizard.test.mjs:3723 is the executable form of this boundary and is a required green criterion at EVERY step. If R5/R6 ever make it fail, the floor is over-firing and the change is wrong. Review turns are specifically excluded because "do something anyway" on a review would silently replace a child's build - the verdict gate at 5086-5096 still fails closed.

The turn body's seven shared mutables (answer/selectedAction/responseMode/providerGoal/providerActionAccepted/contractCaveat/title) are read and rewritten out of order across ~350 lines. classifyAction is called re-entrantly and with a filtered history in three places (1926, 2994, 144) and is also the recovery ladder's planner (5077) and the intent oracle for provider actions (3428). designs.thesis:
The reported failure is not an evaluation gap, it is a GATING gap: every contract check, repair round, and "never do nothing" floor in ask() is guarded by `buildRequest` (wizard.mjs:5097, 5174, 5179), and `isBuildRequest` (1980-1994) returns false for "clear a 50x50 area around me". With buildRequest=false and classifyAction returning null (verified empirically), the #44 promise/refusal ladder at 5074-5085 throws into the universal offline catch (5156-5166), which assigns `selectedAction = safeFallback.action` = null. Wiz stands still. Fix the gate, not the gatekeepers.

The restructure is therefore a THIN ORCHESTRATOR: a new `src/orchestrator.mjs` that owns an explicit, budgeted state machine over the planning phase only (today's wizard.mjs:4924-5203), driven by injected role closures that are literally today's validated functions. Intake, retrieval, preference isolation, goal derivation, sequence/supersede discipline, persistence, and response assembly stay exactly where they are and are not touched. No validated predicate is reimplemented; the orchestrator only decides WHICH role runs next and asserts an invariant at the terminal state.

Three concrete behavioural changes ride on that skeleton:
(1) a new `isActionableRequest` predicate — broader than isBuildRequest, meaning "the child asked for something to happen in the world" — becomes the gate for evaluation + escalation, so terrain/clear/level/administrative turns get the same never-empty treatment build turns already get;
(2) a new deterministic planner rung `terrainEditAction` (src/world-edit.mjs) that compiles "clear/level a WxD area" into a chunked fill-with-air `run_commands` action — which I verified already passes allowedWizardAction, providerPowerMatchesRequest's guarded-fill intent table (wizard.mjs:3341-3345, needs clear|remove|delete|destroy|erase|demolish|break|dig|excavate in the question — "clear" is present), and providerActionMatchesRequest's run_commands equality rule (3429-3441);
(3) a terminal OFFER floor plus a machine-checked invariant: an actionable turn may never terminate with `action===null` AND an answer that promises or refuses. It must terminate with an executable action, or with a single concrete offer that `answerOffersAction` matches and `boundPendingOffer` can bind on the next "yes".

The never-empty property becomes provable by construction at the loop level rather than emergent from 350 lines of interleaved `if`s: the state machine has exactly one terminal state, and that state runs an assertion that swaps in the canned offer if the invariant is violated.

The failure is not "no evaluator before execution" — it is that every quality gate and every never-give-up floor in ask() is guarded by `buildRequest`, and terrain/administrative/effect requests have `buildRequest === false` by construction. Fix it by extracting five typed roles behind an explicit orchestrator turn loop whose escalation ladder is INTENT-CLASSED rather than build-only, and whose terminal rung is guaranteed non-empty.

THE DESIGN: do not add a second opinion. Split the opinion that already exists into severity tiers, make the floor keyed on a generalized `actionableIntent` instead of `buildRequest`, and let the orchestrator adjudicate planner-vs-critic by shipping partial credit into the world rather than buying another provider round. The critic is deterministic in tiers C0–C3 and adds zero provider cost; optional model critique (C4) is asymmetric — it can only downgrade an accept, never upgrade a safety reject — and shares the existing repair wall-clock rather than stacking on it.
